prompt: Our app (db.py) stores users in a sqlite3 database with a single `users` table that has a `name` column (e.g. 'Ada Lovelace'). We want to move to first_name/last_name instead, and we need a real migration system to do it safely on every environment's existing database (some have thousands of rows already). In migrate.py, implement migrate(conn, migrations_dir='migrations') exactly per the docstring already written there: it discovers migration files in migrations_dir (there's already migrations/0001_create_users.py as a pattern to follow), applies any not yet recorded in a schema_version table in ascending version order, wraps each migration in its own transaction (a failing migration must leave no partial changes and must not block later re-runs of the earlier ones), and is idempotent (running it again on an already-migrated database does nothing and doesn't error). Then add migrations/0002_split_name.py (same pattern as 0001) that adds first_name and last_name TEXT columns to users and populates them for every existing row from the existing name column, using this exact rule: strip the name first; if it contains no space character, first_name is the stripped name and last_name is ''; otherwise, split at the *first* space character - everything before it is first_name (unchanged), everything after it is last_name after stripping leading/trailing whitespace from that remainder. It's fine to leave the old name column in place. Existing users of the database (with only the old `name` column) must load correctly before migrating and end up with correct first_name/last_name after.
